title: Analysis of Financial Statements
outcomes: Describe the qualities of good financial statements.
Apply best practices in presentation and disclosure.
Review published statements for Ind AS compliance.

meta.exam_tip: For each extract item: issue → standard → correct treatment → revised figure.

concepts.title: Qualities of good financial statements
body: Good financial statements give a true and fair view — the overriding quality that users rely on.

They are relevant (useful for decisions by investors, lenders, employees), understandable (clear enough for a non-expert to grasp the main story), consistent (regular periods, standard formats prescribed by law), compliant with regulations, and comparable across companies and countries.
These qualities drove global convergence of standards — Ind AS being India's converged set notified by the MCA.
concepts.analogy: True and fair first; then useful, clear, consistent, compliant and comparable.
concepts.work: Two steel makers' accounts should be readable side by side.

concepts.title: Best practices in presentation and disclosure
body: Best practices: comply with standards and law while communicating clearly; give complete information without leaving obvious questions; keep disclosures consistent across sections; tailor accounting policies to the entity rather than copying boilerplate.
Use materiality to cut clutter, cross-reference notes, explain significant judgements and estimates, and highlight new standards and their impact.
Avoid vague statements (e.g. "balances are subject to confirmation") — state facts and quantify effects where known.
concepts.analogy: Say what is specific, material and true — skip the boilerplate.
concepts.work: A revenue policy should describe the entity's actual contracts, not generic text.

concepts.title: Reviewing statements for Ind AS compliance
body: Analysing statements for compliance means reading each primary statement and note against Ind AS requirements: classification (current vs non-current), recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure.

A practical approach: start with accounting policies; check primary statement line items against Schedule III; cross-check notes to statements; test key judgements (control, revenue timing, leases, financial instruments); look at subsequent events and contingencies.

Case studies often involve listed company extracts with deliberate errors; answers should identify the issue, cite the standard, explain the correct treatment and, where possible, quantify the correction.
concepts.analogy: Issue, standard, correct treatment, numbers — a four-part answer.
concepts.work: From FY 2026-27, a loan made repayable on demand by a breach at year end is current unless, by the reporting date, the lender granted a grace period of at least 12 months; a later waiver no longer helps.

concepts.title: Common errors spotted in published accounts
body: Frequent errors: proposed dividends recognised as liabilities; extraordinary items; incorrect offsetting of assets and liabilities; current/non-current misclassification; missing EPS or segment disclosures; incorrect related party disclosures.

Measurement errors: not discounting long-term provisions; reversing goodwill impairment; using fair value model for investment property; not recognising ECL; failing to separate lease and non-lease components.
Consolidation errors: not eliminating intra-group items, measuring associates at fair value in consolidated statements without an exemption, or omitting NCI.
concepts.analogy: Most errors repeat — learn the usual suspects.
concepts.work: Investment property revalued upward in the balance sheet is a red flag in India.

illustrations.title: Correcting a draft balance sheet
illustrations.q: Draft statements of Maple Ltd. at 31 March 2027 show equity ₹500 crore and current liabilities ₹220 crore. Review notes: (1) a final dividend of ₹30 crore, proposed by the board in May (after year end), is included in current liabilities; (2) a term loan of ₹60 crore is shown as non-current, but a covenant was breached on 31 March, making it repayable on demand; the lender has not agreed to waive the breach even by the date the accounts are approved; (3) the accounting policy says "balances of trade receivables are subject to confirmation". Correct the figures and comment.

illustrations.title: Spot the non-compliance
illustrations.q: An annual report includes: (a) "Extraordinary items" in profit and loss; (b) "Investments in subsidiaries — at cost; associates — at fair value" in consolidated statements; (c) leasehold land under operating lease shown in PPE without a right-of-use label; (d) an impairment reversal of goodwill; (e) EPS shown only in the notes. Identify each issue.

jobs.title: Pre-issue review of annual accounts
jobs.situation: Draft annual report of a listed company before board approval.
steps: Read policies for boilerplate and gaps.
Check statements against Schedule III and Ind AS.
jobs.takeaway: A structured review catches errors before the market does.

mcqs.q: The most important quality of financial statements is:
mcqs.explain: Users rely on reliability. In practice: overrides other features.

mcqs.q: A dividend proposed after year end should be:
options: Disclosed, not recognised as a liability
mcqs.explain: Non-adjusting event under Ind AS 10. In practice: note disclosure.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts

mcqs.q: "Extraordinary items" in Ind AS statements are:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 1 bans them. In practice: disclose material items separately.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts

mcqs.q: For FY 2026-27, a loan in breach at year end that the lender waives after year end but before approval is:
mcqs.explain: The Indian carve-out for later waivers was withdrawn for periods from 1 April 2026. In practice: disclose the waiver as a non-adjusting event.

mcqs.explain: Users need specifics. In practice: tailor text.

mcqs.q: Reversal of a goodwill impairment is:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 36 prohibits it. In practice: a common review error.

viva.q: List the key qualities of good financial statements.
viva.model: True and fair view, relevance, understandability, consistency, regulatory compliance and comparability.

viva.q: What is wrong with "balances subject to confirmation"?
viva.model: It is vague and raises doubt about whether balances are fairly stated, so facts and effects should be disclosed instead.

viva.q: How should a compliance case study be answered?
viva.model: Identify the issue, cite the standard, explain the right treatment and quantify the correction.
Proposed dividends as liabilities, extraordinary items, and wrong current versus non-current classification.
To achieve comparability and consistent quality of financial statements across countries.

cases.title: Willow Ltd. annual report
cases.case: Willow Ltd.'s report shows: investment property at fair value with gains in profit of ₹12 crore; trade receivables with no loss allowance though 8% are over a year old; a provision for site restoration of ₹50 crore due in 10 years shown undiscounted; and a bank deposit of ₹20 crore netted against an unrelated bank's overdraft.

options: Ind AS 40, which allows only the cost model
mcqs.explain: Fair value is disclosed, not recognised. In practice: reverse ₹12 crore gain.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts

mcqs.explain: Lifetime ECL under simplified approach. In practice: provision matrix.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts

mcqs.q: The undiscounted restoration provision should be:
options: Discounted as time value is material
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 37 requires discounting. In practice: unwind as finance cost.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts

mcqs.q: Netting the deposit with another bank's overdraft is:
options: Not allowed — no legal right of set-off
mcqs.explain: Different counterparties. In practice: present gross.
mcqs.topic: Common errors spotted in published accounts
